theories.claim: copyBoundedTree has a TOCTOU window between the directory walk that rejects symlinks, special files, and hardlinks and the subsequent os.Open that materializes each file, allowing a concurrent source-tree mutation to substitute a symlink or hardlink for a regular file and bypass the security checks.
theories.basis: isolation.go:320-365 walks the source with filepath.WalkDir and rejects entries based on entry.Info() (cached from the directory read). isolation.go:436-449 then opens each file by path with os.Open, which follows symlinks. There is no os.Lstat or mode or link-count re-check between the two steps, and readRegularFile only verifies that read length matches the cached Size. The walk callback link-count check uses the cached Stat_t from the directory entry, not a fresh lstat of the path about to be opened.
theories.verification_surface: isolation.go:317-371 copyBoundedTree, isolation.go:436-450 readRegularFile, isolation_test.go:55-86 TestIsolationRejectsEscapeSymlinkSpecialHardlinkAndBudgets which does not exercise a TOCTOU substitution.
theories.confirmation_condition: Code review confirms that the only file-type and link-count inspection happens in the WalkDir callback and that os.Open in readRegularFile does not re-stat the path; the existing test suite never substitutes a regular file with a symlink during the copy.
theories.refutation_condition: readRegularFile re-stats with os.Lstat or equivalent and re-checks symlink and hardlink invariants before writing, or the workspace is created from a path the caller already proved unmodifiable.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Whether a real caller can mutate the source during CreateIsolation depends on the operator and OS, neither of which is observable from this read-only review.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Read isolation.go:317-450 and isolation_test.go:55-86 to confirm there is no re-check after os.Open and that the rejection tests construct the symlink and hardlink before CreateIsolation starts. Do not invoke CreateIsolation with a mutating source.

theories.claim: Directory entries are masked to 0o700 during copy, but regular-file entries are written with their original Mode().Perm() bits intact, so a source file with group- or world-writable permissions such as 0666 or 0777 survives verbatim into the isolated workspace and weakens the 0700 containment promised by the parent directory.
theories.basis: isolation.go:346 masks directory mode with info.Mode().Perm() and 0o700 when calling os.Mkdir. isolation.go:357 then calls os.WriteFile(destination, data, info.Mode().Perm()) with no masking. isolation.go:105 creates the parent at 0o700, but the copied file mode is independent of the parent directory mode on POSIX.
theories.verification_surface: isolation.go:344-359 the divergent os.Mkdir and os.WriteFile calls in copyBoundedTree, isolation.go:105 parent directory mode, isolation_test.go:13-53 which exercises no test with a non-0o600 source mode.
theories.confirmation_condition: Line-by-line comparison shows directories are masked with and 0o700 while files are written with raw Perm(); no test or call site normalises source file modes before copy.
theories.refutation_condition: isolation.go applies a and 0o700 mask or equivalent before os.WriteFile, or the caller is required to pre-chmod the source tree.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Whether the workspace parent mode 0o700 plus typical source mode 0o644 produces a practical exploit depends on the deployment environment, which is out of scope for this packet.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Read isolation.go:344-359 and confirm the asymmetry between the Mkdir mask and the WriteFile call. Do not attempt to copy a non-default-mode file tree.

theories.claim: Cleanup uses a non-atomic os.RemoveAll followed by os.Lstat to confirm deletion, so any process or attacker that recreates the workspace path between the two syscalls produces a false-positive workspace still exists error and a blocked outcome even though the original cleanup succeeded.
theories.basis: isolation.go:248-260: RemoveAll is called, then Lstat is used to verify absence. There is no rename-then-rm or fd-based unlink. internal/sprint/qa_investigation.go:132-136 promotes any cleanup_uncertain to QAEvidenceBlocked, so a transient recreate propagates as a blocked evidence record.
theories.verification_surface: isolation.go:242-262 Cleanup, internal/sprint/qa_investigation.go:132-140 consumer that maps CleanupResult.Complete==false to Blocked.
theories.confirmation_condition: CleanupResult reports Error=workspace still exists or Complete==false when no QA-relevant files remain but the path was briefly re-created; consumer logic maps this to a blocked evidence outcome.
theories.refutation_condition: Cleanup uses an atomic compare-and-delete such as rename plus rm or the consumer distinguishes recreated by another process from incomplete remove.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Whether a recreate race actually occurs depends on concurrent host activity, which cannot be observed from a static review.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Read isolation.go:242-262 and internal/sprint/qa_investigation.go:132-140 to confirm the non-atomic verification and the Blocked promotion. Do not race Cleanup against a competing mkdir.
